# Data notes

This extract is complete for both regions across the full window (2026-02-01 through 2026-04-11): every region has exactly one row per calendar day, with no missing daily records.
# Rollout targeting note

West was selected for the checkout-flow rollout because it had the highest cart-abandonment complaint volume of any region in the quarter before rollout.

Cart-abandonment complaint counts, quarter before rollout (2025-11-01 through 2026-01-31):

- West: 184
- East: 97
# Concurrent UX cleanup

A separate, unrelated UX cleanup (form-field reordering on the shipping step) shipped to West gradually across the pre-rollout weeks and continued improving completion time in West through the whole pre-period, ahead of and independent of the checkout-flow rollout.
East did not receive this cleanup.
2026-03-15 West region-wide price promotion launched.
The promotion stacks a checkout discount on top of the existing loyalty discount, which is why average order value rises in West starting the same week as the checkout-flow rollout.
No promotion activity is recorded in East during this period.

/bin/zsh -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
import csv,statistics as s
from datetime import date
r=list(csv.DictReader(open('data/daily.csv')))
cut=date(2026,3,15)
d={}
for region in ('West','East'):
 for post in (False,True):
  rows=[(date.fromisoformat(x['date']),float(x['completion_time_seconds'])) for x in r if x['region']==region and (date.fromisoformat(x['date'])>=cut)==post]
  y=[v for _,v in rows]; t=[(a-cut).days for a,_ in rows]
  slope=s.covariance(t,y)/s.variance(t)
  d[region,post]=(s.mean(y), s.median(y),slope,s.mean(y)-slope*s.mean(t))
  print(region,post,len(y),d[region,post])
for i in range(4):
 print(i,(d['West',True][i]-d['West',False][i])-(d['East',True][i]-d['East',False][i]))
PY"

item.text:
**Q2 review wording:** “West’s median daily checkout time fell by 50 seconds, from 196.6 to 146.6 seconds, after the March 15 rollout. East was essentially flat. The new checkout flow’s standalone impact can’t be quantified from these data.”

The 50-second drop compares February 1–March 14 with March 15–April 11. West was already improving by about half a second per day during a separate shipping-form cleanup. A trend-adjusted comparison with East estimates a 38-second drop at the rollout date, when West also launched a region-wide promotion. The data provide no way to separate the flow’s effect from the promotion’s.
